title: Acute neurological deterioration
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Fictional scenario specification; never imported, published or shown to learners.
learning_objectives: Record the three GCS responses separately with the total, and compare with the baseline.
Report a deterioration promptly, giving most attention to the motor response.
Return to the more frequent observation schedule after a deterioration.
Recognise that neurosurgical discussion and imaging are medical decisions.

sources.use: NICE NG232 (2023): GCS recording, observation, neurosurgical discussion triggers
ACS 2024 TBI Table 10, printed page 87, serial components/pupil monitoring and urgent repeat imaging after neurological decline

required_sources: Unit observation chart, frequency and escalation policy
Licence for reproducing GCS wording (not requested)
gaps: No published clinical scenario may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The branching content, consequences and scoring are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical review.

NICE NG232 covers people with a head injury, mainly in emergency departments and early hospital care; the scenario is framed as a fictional head-injured patient and is not evidence for other causes of neurological deterioration.
Numerical triggers, observation intervals and imaging criteria in NG232 are deliberately not used.
ACS 2024 TBI-specific serial assessment and urgent repeat imaging recommendations now linked. Causes and treatment of nontraumatic deterioration remain outside this case.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register for each source's reproduction status.
NICE: Notice of rights not read; GCS wording is copyright; paraphrase only.
setting: A fictional adult admitted after a head injury, on a fictional unit with a head injury observation chart.

steps.info: At a routine check the patient responds less than at the last check, and the best motor response is lower than before.

options.text: Stay with the patient, assess airway, breathing and circulation, and activate urgent clinical reassessment for new neurological deterioration. In parallel, record eye, verbal and motor responses separately with the total where assessable, compare with baseline, and communicate the changes.
options.feedback: NICE NG232 prioritises urgent reassessment for deteriorating neurological signs. Do not wait for repeated scoring before escalating an unstable patient; record the assessable GCS components and explain factors limiting assessment. For head injury observations include pupil size and reactivity, limb movement and vital signs. New pupil inequality or asymmetric movement merits urgent reassessment. Check and document factors such as intubation, sedation or paralysis; if any GCS component is non-testable, do not invent a score or calculate a misleading total. ACS 2024 supports repeated standardized examinations and documentation, including individual responses and pupils, while protecting hemodynamics and gas exchange.
options.consequence: The clinician is told promptly and the full component record is available.

options.text: Record only the total score and check again at the usual time.
options.feedback: NICE says the components must always accompany the total, and a deterioration should be reported without waiting.
options.consequence: The change in the motor response is lost in the total and the report is delayed.

options.text: Assume the patient is tired and let them sleep without further checks.
options.feedback: A fall in responsiveness is a deterioration to report, not to assume away.

steps.info: The clinician has been told and is on the way. Observations were due at a longer interval.
steps.prompt: How should you observe the patient now?

options.text: Maintain bedside assessment and the emergency team's observation plan. Return to the intensified observation schedule for deterioration, record changes, and escalate again if airway, breathing, circulation or neurological status worsens.
options.feedback: NICE says to revert to the most frequent observation schedule for a person who deteriorates and to document on a standard head injury proforma. Maintain patient-specific observation and escalation; do not generalize the NICE head injury schedule to every cause of ICU neurological deterioration.
options.consequence: The observations show the trend and the clinician arrives to a complete record.

options.text: Keep the longer interval because the clinician is already coming.
options.feedback: The schedule is shortened after a deterioration, whoever is on the way.
options.consequence: A further change between checks is missed.

options.text: Stop GCS checks and watch the monitor numbers instead.
options.feedback: Monitor numbers do not replace the GCS observations.
options.consequence: The neurological trend is no longer recorded.

steps.info: The team decides to involve the neurosurgical team and arrange imaging. The family asks what is happening.

observations.label: Neurosurgical team
observations.value: To be contacted by the clinician

options.text: Keep observing and recording, give a clear handover of the trend, support the team with preparation, and tell the family what the team has agreed to share without giving a diagnosis yourself.
options.feedback: Discussing care with a neurosurgeon and deciding on imaging are medical decisions; the nurse's role is to observe, record, communicate the trend and support the team. In a patient with traumatic brain injury and a worsening examination, ACS 2024 supports urgent repeat head CT. Prepare transport and ongoing monitoring with the clinical team rather than delaying escalation for a routine scan slot.
options.consequence: The team has the information it needs and the family has been kept informed within agreed limits.

options.text: Contact the scanner and arrange the scan yourself without waiting for the clinician.
options.feedback: Decisions about imaging and neurosurgical discussion belong to the medical team.
options.consequence: The pathway is confused and the team has to undo the booking.

options.text: Tell the family what you think is wrong with the patient.
options.feedback: Diagnosis is for the responsible clinician; the nurse shares only what the team has agreed.
options.consequence: The family receives an unconfirmed explanation.

learning_points: Record individual assessable eye, verbal and motor responses, pupil findings and limb movements; compare with baseline. If a GCS component is non-testable, document why and omit a misleading total.

Escalate new neurological deterioration urgently, including pupil inequality, new focal asymmetry or a fall in motor response. Continue the diagnosis-specific intensified observation plan without waiting for repeat scoring.
Neurosurgical discussion and imaging are medical decisions; observe, record, hand over and support.
For traumatic brain injury with worsening examination, communicate urgency of clinician-directed repeat imaging and maintain appropriate monitoring during transport.
